prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Sentinel Vale EO ground segment. Security: least privilege, strong auth, segmentation, audit. Mission Control Center (MCC, Bluebell): real-time ops, anomaly response, releases validated commands, owns contact schedule/routing; elevated access needs approved shift role+time-limited need; sends constraints to MPS; escalation lead→discipline lead→mission mgmt; declares continuity modes after consulting technical leads, recording objective, duration, exit criteria. Modes: monitor-only (command release stopped, telemetry continues where safe, protect evidence); essential-service (safety contacts, time-critical telemetry, core orbit support, protect unrecoverable payload data). Flight Dynamics Facility (FDF, Mistral): orbit catalog; ephemerides/events (validity, frame, generation time, use statement) to MCC, MPS, PPF; Star Tracker Mask File; Ephemeris Delta Note; maneuver recs to Spacecraft Operations Team (SOT); geometry to Payload Calibration Team (PCT); Orbit Determination Engine. Payload Processing Facility (PPF, Forgehouse): Primary/Backup Processing Clusters; Primary may pause nonessential queues for validated recovery runs; transfer to Backup only after custody, software baseline, operator authorization verified; both down→suspend, stage raw, notify MCC; quarantines suspect input/output if lineage unproven. Telemetry Ingest Service; Pass Replay Packet (SOT). L0–L2 record versions. PCT owns calibration baseline, requests reprocessing. Product Quality Service: quality flags, Product Hold List, reprocessing reason. Long Term Archive (Granite): authoritative custody reference incl. degraded ops; admits after PPF package+quality metadata+checksum; Storage Watermark Snapshot; catalogue to User Services Portal; reconciles delayed ingest/publication before normal status. User Services Portal: versioned contracts; reports confirmed impacts, no speculative root cause before incident lead approval. Cybersecurity Desk: security coordination. Network Control System (Lantern): routing, Security Exception Ticket. Mission Planning System (MPS, Cedar): command package to MCC; suspends auto schedule publication in security/continuity anomalies. Command Validation Gateway (Osprey): mask file checks. Ground Network Manager: coordinates cross-site failover (antennas, routing, firewall, schedules); antennas: North S-Band, South S-Band, Kiruna X-Band, Svalbard X-Band. Triage: preserve logs/config/console history/message IDs before restarts; evidence in write-protected case storage with chain

Document units:
S228: The readiness review board verifies that each open action from launch and commissioning has an owner, a due date, and an accepted residual risk statement where closure is not required before service start.
S229: Acceptance evidence is drawn from end-to-end rehearsals, procedure dry runs, interface verification records, capacity tests, security monitoring checks, and operator training completion records.
S230: The Mission Control Center demonstrates continuous console coverage for the agreed service hours and proves that shift handover logs contain the state needed by the incoming controller.
S231: The Flight Dynamics Facility provides readiness evidence showing that orbit products, maneuver screening, and conjunction coordination can be performed within the committed planning cycle.
S232: The Payload Processing Facility demonstrates that science product generation can be sustained during representative contact patterns without manual intervention beyond approved operator actions.
S233: The Network Control System records rehearsal outcomes for planned maintenance, station loss, degraded routing, and restoration of nominal connectivity after a simulated outage.
S234: The Ground Network Manager accepts the antenna readiness baseline only when the North S-Band Antenna, South S-Band Antenna, Kiruna X-Band Antenna, and Svalbard X-Band Antenna have current maintenance clearances.
S235: The Spacecraft Operations Team conducts at least one integrated day-in-the-life rehearsal that includes pass preparation, commanding discipline, telemetry surveillance, anomaly declaration, and recovery reporting.
S236: The Flight Dynamics Team conducts a separate rehearsal for missed tracking data and late orbit update availability to confirm that planning products remain usable under degraded conditions.
S237: The Payload Calibration Team validates that calibration operations are represented in the rehearsal schedule and that product quality decisions can be traced to approved engineering criteria.
S238: The Cybersecurity Desk participates in the final exercise by validating alert routing, privileged access review, and incident coordination with operations management.
S239: The User Services Portal uses the Product Hold List to prevent release of affected products until the applicable hold condition has been cleared.
S240: The Mission Planning System applies the delta note during schedule validation to ensure that contact and activity timing remains consistent with the latest operational constraint.
S241: The Backup Processing Cluster uses the Storage Watermark Snapshot to verify that recovery capacity is sufficient before it accepts routine standby responsibility.
S242: Osprey rejects any command request that lacks the approved authorization state, validation result, and operator acknowledgment required for routine service.
S243: Granite preserves the accepted archive baseline and confirms that retrieval tests meet the service objective before routine operations are declared stable.
